payload.title: Wedding in Crete Guide to Seasons, Venues and Costs
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, planning 60 to 150 guests flying in from Australia. Crete is on their shortlist, perhaps against Santorini or Italy, and they are now planning or comparing: which months work, which end of the island suits their guests, what actually moves the cost and how far ahead the paperwork must start. They want one clear page that answers those questions before they spend time on individual venue quotes.
payload.goal: Book a Wedded Concierge consultation (speak with a Wedded Advisor) at /wonderland-concierge.
payload.angle: Crete is not one wedding destination but two: the resort coast of Elounda and Agios Nikolaos in the east, and the harbour towns and smaller, more personal venues of Rethymno and Chania in the west, with Heraklion between them. Page-one results treat the island as a single backdrop and quote prices that date quickly. This guide plans a Crete wedding the way an Australian couple has to: season by month from official climate data and the windows venues themselves state, the right end of the island for where guests will land, a short east-to-west run of real venues, the cost drivers written as questions to ask (no figures, so it stays true), and document lead times from the Embassy and venue terms set into a working timeline.
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words: Crete suits a late-spring to early-autumn wedding, east for resorts and west for harbour towns and smaller venues, with costs driven by season, guest rooms, exclusive use and what sits outside a package; link /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-venues prominently and the hub /destinations/europe/greece.
Exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways, no figures.

When to marry: seasons month by month from official sources only (hnms.gr, meteo.gr, visitgreece.gr, incrediblecrete.gr) plus venue-stated season windows and ceremony times; Smartraveller heat and wildfire advice dated once.

Choosing an area and a venue: east vs centre vs west in short, venue types (resort, chapel, estate or garden), then 6 example venues east to west with one line each: Elounda Beach Hotel & Villas (Elounda), St. Nicolas Bay Resort Hotel & Villas (Agios Nikolaos), Amirandes, Grecotel (Heraklion coast), Caramel, Grecotel (Rethymno), Avra Imperial (Kolymvari), Sea View by En Kipo (Chania); each line reuses facts already in the venues guide source pack; then link the venues guide for the full 15.

What drives the cost, with no prices or amounts: season and date, guest numbers and room blocks or minimum nights, exclusive use, venue hire vs package, extras priced separately, guest travel to the venue, documents; each written as a question to ask the venue, only where venue terms support it; link /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages.
Getting there and getting around: Heraklion and Chania airports and which end of the island each serves, drive times only as venues state them; no transfer arrangements offered.

Legal in brief as at November 2026: one short paragraph from Embassy Athens and Smartraveller plus the Elounda Collection document steps and 40-day registration as sourced; link the Greece guide legal section; nothing on church or religious paperwork.

Planning timeline anchored only on sourced lead times (documents, registration, venue season), with a Concierge invitation after it; FAQ of 5 to 6 questions; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once and /magazine once.
avoid: Any price, fee, euro or AUD figure, 'from' price or percentage anywhere, including FAQ, meta and takeaways.
Repeating the venues guide: no more than one line per venue, no capacity tables, no venue beyond the 6 named examples.

Research talk in copy (what we could or could not find, trace or confirm; sources or method; 'you will often read'; myths sections); per-line source credits; hedge stacking; 'often told' more than once.
Stating a custom's meaning or origin as fact; anything on legal, church or religious paperwork beyond the brief legal summary; any Advisor role in paperwork.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, review sites or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images.
Vendor names other than the example venues; venue contact or business details; transfer arrangements; implied partnerships.
Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; 'from first idea to the last dance', 'last dance'.
Ranking venues or areas as 'best'; weather claims not from an official source.
Cliches, exclamation marks, pasted or bracketed keywords in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.

payload.intro_plan: Open on the reader's decision (Crete is on the shortlist and they need to know when, where and what drives the cost), give the direct answer in the first 100 words, then link the Crete venues guide and the Greece hub.
key_takeaways_plan: Late spring and early autumn give the easiest balance of warm weather and comfortable ceremony times on Crete.
The east suits resort weddings near Heraklion airport, while Rethymno and Chania suit harbour towns and smaller venues.
Season, guest rooms, exclusive use and what sits outside a package drive the cost more than the venue name does.
Start your documents early, because Greek registration has fixed lead times that set the rest of the timeline.
